justice: The complete lack of sidewalks and tactile paving severely restricts accessibility and fairness for wheelchair users and the visually impaired.
The entire paved surface is dedicated to mixed traffic without protected zones, showing poor equity in spatial distribution for pedestrians and cyclists.
The absence of curb ramps or safe refuge areas creates a discriminatory physical environment that fails to accommodate elderly and disabled road users.
safety: The lack of physical separation, such as curbs or bollards, between vehicles and vulnerable road users (youth, elderly) creates high collision risks.
Prominent longitudinal cracks sealed with tar in the asphalt surface pose tripping hazards for pedestrians and stability risks for cyclists.
The visible metal guardrails on both sides effectively provide edge protection to prevent vehicles and users from falling off the elevated road.
The absence of visible street lighting installations raises significant concerns for nighttime visibility and safety for all road users.
livability: The total absence of surrounding buildings, ground-floor commercial units, or community facilities fails to provide street vitality or meet daily needs.
The lack of street furniture, such as benches or resting pavilions, offers no support for older adults or persons with physical limitations who need frequent breaks.
The purely utilitarian road design, bordered only by natural vegetation and guardrails, discourages social interaction or community presence for all age groups.
sustainability: The absence of dedicated bus lanes or protected bike lanes fails to provide infrastructure that encourages sustainable, low-carbon transportation modes.
The continuous sealed asphalt surface lacks visible sustainable urban drainage systems (SUDS) or permeable paving for effective stormwater management.
While the surrounding off-road areas feature natural vegetation, the built road infrastructure itself lacks integrated street trees or green buffers.
aesthetics: Long, highly visible sealed cracks running down the center of the asphalt detract significantly from the visual quality of the road surface.
The bare metal guardrails and lack of any decorative architectural elements create a monotonous and strictly utilitarian visual environment.
The adjacent natural tree canopy and open agricultural fields provide some visual relief, though the built roadway itself remains unappealing.
comfort: The complete lack of street trees or artificial shading structures on the roadway exposes pedestrians and cyclists to harsh sun, reducing thermal comfort, especially for the elderly.
The absence of any benches or resting facilities makes walking physically demanding and uncomfortable for socially vulnerable groups.
Sharing a relatively narrow, unseparated roadway with motor vehicles induces significant psychological stress and acoustic discomfort for pedestrians and cyclists.
walkability: The absolute absence of dedicated sidewalks forces pedestrians, including children and seniors, to walk directly on the vehicle roadway, severely compromising walkability.
The lack of pedestrian crossings, tactile paving, or wayfinding signage makes the route highly unnavigable and unsafe for disabled walkers.
The unbroken length of the exposed road without resting spots or shade creates a hostile and exhausting walking environment.
bikeability: The lack of dedicated or painted bike lanes forces cyclists to share the lane with motor vehicles, reducing perceived and actual safety for youth and elderly cyclists.
The prominent tar-sealed cracks along the road surface can catch narrow bicycle tires, presenting a physical hazard that hinders smooth riding.
The absence of traffic calming measures or clear lane markings on this open stretch of road increases the risk of high-speed vehicular conflicts for cyclists.
